scope: Independent local raw-result, commandstats, checkpoint, state, monitor and provenance cross-check; no remote actions or new benchmark runs.

identity.archive_binary_limit: Binary identity is verified through collected build/runtime hash attestations; binaries are not included in the local result archive.

interpretation_limits: Single round per command, compared with the earlier fixed main 684894d run; no randomized alternation or repeated-run uncertainty estimate. Small throughput/tail differences are observations, not proof of stable improvement or regression.
The measured candidate is the combined optimization stack d0084f4, including PR357 48ca16c and prior ZSet changes; this experiment does not isolate the marginal effect of each patch.

Each family recovered the preceding checkpoint, then explicitly FLUSHDB and freshly loaded 8192 keys. This removes the previous crossover experiment’s second-namespace logical dataset confound, but physical device history was not reset.

CPU is process user+system ticks divided by the actual 45-second monotonic interval and includes storage polling and waiting implementation costs. Lower process CPU is measurable; it is not a direct measure of useful-copy CPU or proof of a particular causal mechanism.

Formal client timing is approximately 60 seconds; CPU/NIC observations cover an interior approximately 45-second interval beginning about 3–4 seconds after launch. Ten-second throughput bins and monitor bins are not treated as exactly synchronized windows. No CPU/NIC trace was captured during warm-up.

TCP counters are host-wide. Accelerated VF and synthetic NIC counters are not added. Rare retransmissions and zero selected-NIC drops/errors do not prove the absence of every possible network disturbance.

Zero grouped transaction admission for load, warm and formal supports the intended compact ZSet path together with the pinned code and 11272-byte encoded page under the 16KiB promotion threshold. It must not be generalized as proof that all structures, including Stream, use the same physical encoding.
For LPUSH/RPOP, ZREM/ZADD and SADD/SREM, reported operation throughput is pairs/s and latency is the measured entire pair. Child command p99.9 values cannot be added.

Every formal 60-second bucket total is 80 lower than the total completed operations because each connection finishes its final in-flight operation after the timing cutoff; QPS uses completed count divided by measured elapsed time.
findings: All 14 completed formal points and all 42 load/warm/formal phases have zero client errors, matching exact server command counts and zero failed/rejected command deltas; recovery/clean-stop generations are 8→9 through 21→22, with every new checkpoint containing 8192 entries.
No abrupt throughput collapse appears in the six 10-second formal means. The largest within-point 10-second max/min spread is approximately 2.800%.
Measured throughput differences range from -1.695% to 2.782%; latency p99.9 increases remain visible for SETRANGE (+6.17%), Stream (+4.13%), and smaller changes in HKEYS/SET/ZINCRBY.

Raw process ticks confirm server CPU reductions in SETRANGE, ZINCRBY, ZREM/ZADD and SADD/SREM. Their networks carry only approximately 50–326 Mbps per direction, with no retransmissions or selected-NIC drops/errors in these four formal observations.

High-volume full reads and SET retain roughly 18–20 Gbps transfer volumes. Formal retransmissions are limited to SMEMBERS server 3, LRANGE server 2, ZRANGE server 6, SET client 160 and Stream client 1; all other observed sides have zero.
